text: Film or DGS number, archive and image numbers for the Folder 1 pages, to settle H-010.

The image or citation behind the 1869 census find, to settle H-007. Part answered at B-023: an image is in hand (D-006-07). Still wanted: the village, house number and archive reference of the sheet, and a sharper copy. B-027: all four Solymos sheets are in hand at full size. Still wanted: the website or archive they were viewed on.
The full register page for the Mihály Demkó entry, with its header, to settle H-015 and confirm the column headings.
What led the owner to the Belža Greek Catholic book, and the full pages with their title, to settle H-018.
Baptisms of Demko children at Viszoka from 1857 to 1873 and from 1883 to 1895, if the owner has them, and any entry for a Maria Demko. Settles H-022, H-023.
The full page for the 1872 entry labelled Anna Demko (D-004-01), to see the note cut off above it.

Michal Duska's marriage to Maria Demko (about 1925 to 1929), or any record that gives his age, birth date or parents: a passenger list, a naturalisation or a Canadian burial record would do. His baptism is now in hand twice over: a Mihály of 6 December 1896 and a Mihály of 3 July 1903. One record with his age chooses between them (H-046, H-047). B-029: the 1937 emigration papers name Michal four times and give no age. Still open. ANSWERED at B-033 by the census of 1930 (D-011-24) and the passenger list (D-006-19).

A second image of the 1877 entry for Szenna 72, or other entries naming the same family, to settle the spelling (H-026). Withdrawn at B-013: settled by comparison with another entry by the same clerk.
Baptisms of Duska children in the Senné Roman Catholic register, 1890 to 1910, and any Duska marriage of 1865 to 1900. Settles H-030, H-035, H-036. Answered in the main by folder F-009 (95 files).

The full row, and the rows below it, for Mihály Duska of 'Bradenville' on the page of the December [1902] baptisms at Solymos (D-007-08), and the certificate or extract it cites. The strip cuts the row in half. It would settle the place, the mother's surname and the date, and so test H-040.

The Reformed marriage and burial registers for Solymos, 1860 to 1910, if the owner has pages from them: to name the fathers of János Dusko and Mihály Dusko (H-042) and to see which of the boys named Mihály lived (H-040, H-041).

For the urbarial tables: (1) a larger copy of Solymos page 27, to settle whether sub-cottar no. 8 is a Duska; (2) the last page of the Szenna table, with the one serf of the widow Turánszky; (3) the date written on the tables, if any; (4) the website and address you took them from.

For the cemetery record FT 01965: which cemetery it is, how you got the printout, and a photograph of the stone if there is one. Any record of Miklós (Nicholas, Mike?) Duska and Anna Hancosek in Canada: marriage, death, a passenger list.

The census sheets of the same count for Senné (Szenna), above all houses 5 and 6, where György Duska the elder and György Duska the younger lived. They would give both men's years and places of birth, and so say whether the Senné Duskas were born at Solymos.

From the 1921 census: the household form or forms for every Duska at Senné (and at Iňačovce), with the summary sheet for the village. One form with Michal on it, giving his date of birth and his father's name, answers the first question on this line. B-032: the same for the census of 1930: the sheet for Maria Duska and her son (Senné 160 or her parents' house at Iňačovce), and any other Duska sheet of Senné. Those sheets give exact dates of birth. B-033: the 1930 sheets for Senné have come and answer it. The 1921 sheets would add little now.

Michal (Mike) Duska's own arrival in Canada, most likely 1929 to 1931: the ship's passenger list or his landing card, and his naturalisation papers if he took citizenship. Each gives his age. Also the Montrose manifest of November 1937 for Maria and Štefan. B-033: a crop of his passenger list is in hand. Still wanted: the whole page, with the ship, the date and the columns for nearest relative and destination.

Two records to close the generation above: the marriage of Michal Duska and Maria Demko, 30 January 1927 (probably in the Greek Catholic book of Iňačovce or the Roman Catholic book of Senné), and the source of the 1892 marriage image (which book, which website), so that the link from András to György Duska and Anna Krak can be cited. B-039: the 1892 marriage now has a volume reference from the Places agent (Prešov no. 1092), so the second half is answered in substance; the image's own source is still welcome.

The original baptism entry of Štefan Duska in the Senné Roman Catholic register, volume IV, page 110, entry 43 of 1929 (the coordinator's RQ-11). It would show whether the register says the 21st, as two extracts do, or the 23rd, as the census and three civil papers do.
